description: Per-assertion review state for the regulatory-shaped text carried by this repository's fixtures. Machine-readable companion to docs/finalization/DATA_REVIEW_BACKLOG.md; validated by scripts/validation/regulatory_review.py. Every entry ships in a pending or synthetic-only state: no assertion here has been verified against an authoritative source, because verifying one requires a qualified human reading the regulation, which this repository cannot do.

status_vocabulary.PENDING_REVIEW: No qualified reviewer has judged this yet. The default, and the only state a new assertion may be created in.
status_vocabulary.VERIFIED_WITH_SOURCE: A named reviewer confirmed it against a citable authoritative source at a named version. Reachable only through regulatory_review.promote_to_verified(), which refuses synthetic placeholders and unresolved licences.
status_vocabulary.SYNTHETIC_ONLY: Confirmed to be a deliberately fabricated placeholder. Terminal, and never a step on the way to real regulatory content.
status_vocabulary.REJECTED: Confirmed wrong and withdrawn from use.
status_vocabulary.BLOCKED_BY_LICENSE: May not be used or redistributed because its licence is unresolved. Reviewing will not unblock it; a separate licence decision is required.

license_vocabulary.UNKNOWN: Redistribution licence not established. Treated as blocking: public availability of a text is not a grant to redistribute it.
license_vocabulary.PUBLIC_USE_OK: Licence confirmed to permit use and redistribution.
license_vocabulary.ATTRIBUTION_REQUIRED: Licence confirmed to permit redistribution with attribution or version labelling.
license_vocabulary.NO_REDISTRIBUTION: Licence confirmed to forbid redistribution of the source text.

entries.standalone_misreading_risk: High. A mg/kg figure attributed to a single uniform standard reads as quotable and is the shape most likely to be pasted out of context.
entries.review_question: Real heavy-metal limits are set per product category and per analyte, not as one uniform figure for all cosmetics. Confirm the actual structure per jurisdiction before any figure is quoted, and confirm whether a uniform statement is misleading rather than merely imprecise.

entries.standalone_misreading_risk: High. Asking for a maximum concentration presupposes that one exists; the presupposition is the misreading risk, independent of the number.
entries.review_question: Confirm whether niacinamide appears on any restricted-ingredient list in the target jurisdiction. If it does not, the fixture's question shape itself invites the model to invent a limit.

entries.standalone_misreading_risk: High. Two-tier leave-on / rinse-off framing mirrors a real regulatory pattern, so it reads as plausible while every number is invented.
entries.review_question: Confirm the current retinol concentration limit and the product categories it applies to, and whether children's cosmetics are treated separately.

entries.standalone_misreading_risk: Medium. The subject is a genuinely regulated ingredient, so a reader who checks one figure may assume the rest are sound.
entries.review_question: Confirm the current salicylic acid limit and whether separate limits apply to children's cosmetics in the target jurisdiction.

entries.standalone_misreading_risk: High per row, low by volume. MIT's status differs sharply between jurisdictions, so a single figure invites a confidently wrong cross-market answer.
entries.review_question: Confirm the current restricted-use and prohibited status of methylisothiazolinone per jurisdiction before any limit is stated; a single global figure is the specific failure to avoid.

entries.locator: arbutin: 0015, 0140-0143 (12 measured); kojic acid: 0238; azelaic acid: 0244
entries.standalone_misreading_risk: Medium. Grouped in one fixture family, so a reader may apply one answer to all three.
entries.review_question: Confirm separately for arbutin / alpha-arbutin, kojic acid and azelaic acid whether a limit exists at all and which product categories it covers. Do not carry a finding from one ingredient to another.

entries.standalone_misreading_risk: Medium. A pH range presented in regulatory voice can be confused for a legal limit when it is only a formulation recommendation.
entries.review_question: Determine whether each stated figure is a regulatory limit or a pH-conditioned formulation recommendation, and confirm the distinction is preserved wherever the fixture states it.

entries.standalone_misreading_risk: High. Cites real regulation titles, so it is the most quotable and the most likely to be repeated as an accurate procedural summary.
entries.review_question: Confirm the current regime (filing versus registration, and where the dividing line falls), the material list and the notification-number format, against the regulation itself.

entries.standalone_misreading_risk: High. Four evidence categories read as a direct paraphrase of the regulation's wording.
entries.review_question: Confirm how the efficacy-claim evaluation specification actually enumerates evidence types, and whether the fixture's four-way split matches its wording.

entries.standalone_misreading_risk: Medium. Declining-order labelling and a threshold percentage are common knowledge shaped like a rule, which makes an invented figure hard to spot.
entries.review_question: Confirm the exact current labelling rules on ingredient ordering and any declaration threshold, including whether the threshold figure is jurisdictional.

entries.standalone_misreading_risk: High. Multiplier efficacy claims are prohibited in regulatory contexts, so the fixture asserts something that should not exist at all.
entries.review_question: Recommend deletion rather than correction. Confirm whether any multiplier claim should be removed from the fixtures outright instead of being given a reviewable value.

entries.standalone_misreading_risk: Medium. Citing a real GB series for cosmetic packaging implies the series governs cosmetic packaging, which is the applicability question that is actually unresolved.
entries.review_question: Confirm whether the GB 4806 food-contact series applies to cosmetic primary packaging at all, or only to packaging that shares food-contact use cases. Note this claim appears only in the QLoRA training fixture, not in the retrieval fixtures.

entries.locator: whole file (40 records); training output sidecar offline training_provenance.py
entries.standalone_misreading_risk: High, and it is the one that leaves the machine. The adapter is deployed to a serving stack where the training fixture is not, so a deployed model carries these values with no fixture beside it to qualify them.
entries.review_question: Before any adapter trained on this fixture is exposed to users, confirm what evaluation is intended to stand in for regulatory correctness, and record that evaluation's result. Training convergence is not such an evaluation.

entries.locator: 2 of 12 rows name an instrument; 0 carry a limit-shaped value
entries.standalone_misreading_risk: Low. The set exists to test refusal and fabricated-citation behaviour, so it is read as a test rather than as reference material.
entries.review_question: Confirm the expected refusal behaviour matches the current regulation-citation requirement, so the case does not certify a response pattern that has since changed.

entries.locator: 70 rows; 12 name an instrument, 35 carry a limit-shaped value
entries.standalone_misreading_risk: High. The worksheet is handed to a human reviewer for mapping decisions, and those decisions are the moment a candidate could be mistaken for an approved label.
entries.review_question: Confirm the review protocol tells an annotator that mapping a candidate against the synthetic corpus establishes nothing about regulatory truth, so a completed mapping is not read as verification.
